description: Two transactions read the same row, both write, and the second write silently replaces the first.
A strategy that allows concurrent work and detects a conflict at write time instead of blocking readers.
A JPA attribute that Hibernate compares and increments on every update to detect that the row changed.
An UPDATE whose WHERE clause includes the version read earlier, so zero matched rows means a conflict.
The Spring exception raised when the version no longer matches, which rolls the transaction back.
The HTTP status that tells a client its change clashed with a newer state and must be reloaded.
